title: FS-20 Vortex (Nuclear Option)

sources.title: Nuclear Option 0.34.2 Rewired action catalog (JoyPro DB/NuclearOption/actions.tsv)

intro: The FS-20 Vortex is a fictional single-seat multirole fighter from Nuclear Option that can take off on a short run and land vertically (STOVL). A lift fan behind the cockpit and a swivelling rear nozzle hold it up in the hover. It has a 20 mm cannon and internal bays. All switches sit on the main front panel with three displays.

areas.name: MFDs
areas.text: Three displays on the main front panel.

panels.name: MFDs (multi-function displays)
panels.text: Three screens on the front panel: radar and threats on the left, horizon and heading in the middle, and engine, gear, fuel and targeting on the right.
panels.context: Together they do the jobs of the main and status displays of other aircraft.

controls.name: Left MFD
controls.text: Shows the radar and the threat warnings.
controls.context: The pilot finds targets here and sees which radars are looking at the jet.

controls.name: Centre MFD
controls.text: Shows an artificial horizon and the heading (bearing).
controls.context: It helps the pilot keep the aircraft level in the hover and in clouds.

controls.name: Right MFD
controls.text: Shows the engine, the landing gear, the fuel and the targeting picture.
controls.context: Before a vertical landing the pilot checks gear and fuel here.

areas.name: Stick, throttle and pedals
areas.text: The default joystick map with what is special in this aircraft.

panels.name: Stick
panels.text: The joystick flies the aircraft and holds most of its buttons. Nuclear Option uses one global key map for all aircraft, so every button does the same job in every aircraft.
panels.context: The buttons are named by number because Nuclear Option binds them by joystick button number; on most sticks button 1 is the trigger.

controls.name: Stick axes (pitch, roll, yaw)
controls.text: Pushing the stick forward points the nose down, pulling it points the nose up. Moving it sideways rolls the aircraft. Twisting it (or the rudder pedals) turns the nose left and right (yaw).
controls.context: These are the first axes of the joystick by default; the game's flight computer turns them into movements of the control surfaces.

controls.name: Button 1 (trigger): fire
controls.text: Fires the selected weapon: the gun, a missile, a bomb or a rocket, whichever is selected.
controls.context: The weapon is chosen with button 4; for guided weapons the pilot selects a target first.

controls.name: Button 2: Target Select
controls.text: Selects the unit in the middle of the pilot's view as the target.
controls.context: The pilot looks or points the nose at a unit and presses it; guided weapons then go for that target.

controls.name: Button 3: Target Cancel
controls.text: A short press drops the last selected target. Holding the button clears all targets.
controls.context: Useful after a target is destroyed or when the pilot picked the wrong one.

controls.name: Button 4: Next Weapon
controls.text: A short press steps to the next weapon. Holding the button switches the automatic turret control on or off in aircraft that have a turret.
controls.context: The selected weapon shows on the HUD.

controls.name: Button 5: Next Countermeasure
controls.text: Steps to the next kind of countermeasure, the things the aircraft throws out to fool enemy missiles.
controls.context: Flares fool heat-seeking missiles, chaff fools radar missiles; the pilot picks the right one for the threat.

controls.name: Button 6: Landing gear
controls.text: Raises or lowers the landing gear, the wheels and their legs.
controls.context: Up after take-off for more speed, down before landing; the status display shows the gear position.

controls.name: Button 7: Countermeasures
controls.text: Releases the selected countermeasure, a flare or a bundle of chaff.
controls.context: The pilot presses it when a missile warning sounds, often while turning hard.

controls.name: Button 8: Night vision
controls.text: Switches night vision on or off, which makes the dark visible.
controls.context: It helps on night missions to see the ground and other aircraft.

controls.name: Button 9: Flight assist / auto-hover
controls.text: A short press switches flight assist on or off. In the VTOL aircraft, holding it turns on auto-hover, which keeps the aircraft hovering in place.
controls.context: Flight assist is the flight computer's help that keeps the aircraft smooth and within safe limits.

controls.name: Button 10: Radar
controls.text: Switches the radar on or off. The radar sends radio waves to find other aircraft and units.
controls.context: A radar that is on finds more but also tells the enemy where the aircraft is.

controls.name: Button 11: Eject
controls.text: Ejects the crew: the seats shoot the crew out of the aircraft in an emergency.
controls.context: Used only when the aircraft cannot be saved.

controls.name: Stick grip: the game's flight commands
match: label:Stick grip: the game's flight controls (bind them to any button)
controls.text: In the game's control picture the stick stands for all of Nuclear Option's flight commands, which the player can bind to any button. Besides the defaults above there are commands without a default joystick button, such as Radial Menu, Axis Modifier, Nav Lights, Toggle Engine, Previous Weapon, Link Guns, Weapon Wheel, Turret Control and Custom Axis 1.
controls.context: The same command list applies to every aircraft; the player sets the binds once in the game's control settings.

panels.name: Throttle
panels.text: The throttle lever sets the power of all engines at once, like a car's gas pedal.
panels.context: Nuclear Option reads it from the fourth axis of the device by default; the player binds the real throttle lever there.

controls.name: Throttle axis
controls.text: Forward gives more power to all engines, back gives less.
controls.context: More power means more speed and climb, but also more fuel used and more heat for heat-seeking missiles to follow.

controls.name: Throttle grip: the game's flight commands
match: label:Throttle grip: the game's flight controls (bind them to any button)
controls.text: In the game's control picture the throttle stands for the same list of flight commands as the stick. The player can put any of them, for example Custom Axis 1 or Nav Lights, on the throttle's own buttons and axes.
controls.context: Binds are global in Nuclear Option, so a throttle set up once works in every aircraft.

controls.name: Custom Axis 1 (nozzle and lift fan)
controls.text: Lets the pilot set the nozzle and lift fan by hand instead of the flight computer. It has no default joystick axis; the player binds a slider or wheel (keys Up and Down by default).
controls.context: More downward thrust lifts the jet; turning it back makes it fly forward again.

panels.name: Pedals
panels.text: The brake axis slows the wheels on the ground.
panels.context: By default it is the fifth axis of the device; the player binds a toe brake of the rudder pedals there.

controls.name: Brake axis
controls.text: Pressing the brake slows and stops the aircraft on the ground, harder the further it is pressed.
controls.context: Used after landing and while taxiing; it has no effect in the air.
